newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Indonesia President Suharto in Malaysia for visit.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia President Suharto in Malaysia for visit.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto arrived in Malaysia on Sunday for a two-day visit determined to avoid stirring an old dispute over two islands claimed by both countries, officials said.
Suharto is to hold talks with Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on bilateral, regional and international issues and lunch with King Tuanku Ja'afar, the Indonesian embassy said.
The Indonesian leader, accompanied by a 48-member delegation, was visiting Malaysia at Mahathir's invitation, the national Bernama news agency said.

It said the visit was part of regular bilateral meetings between the two leaders held alternately in Malaysia and Indonesia. The two last met in Bogor, Indonesia, after attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in 1994. Suharto's last visit to Malaysia was in 1993.

Mahathir, who received Suharto on his arrival, had said on Saturday that he and Suharto would avoid raising the subject of the Sipadan and Ligitan islands, which both Malaysia and Indonesia call their own.
Kuala Lumpur has suggested that the dispute over the two islands, located off the coast of Borneo, be referred to the International Court of Justice in The Hague.

Mahathir said his meeting with Suharto would focus on trade and diplomatic matters and their stand on the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), to which both nations belong.
